part.text:
Now I understand the issue. The product page (`app/product/page.tsx:4`) is an async server component that `await`s `getInventory()` at the top level before rendering anything. Since `getInventory()` calls `connection()` (forcing dynamic rendering), the **entire** page — including the static title `

Premium Widget

` — is blocked until the dynamic data resolves. So on navigation, nothing appears until the data is ready. The fix is to split the static title from the dynamic inventory and wrap only the dynamic part in a `` boundary, so the title streams immediately while the inventory loads.
Let me verify the change typechecks correctly.

Typecheck passes. The fix is complete. The problem: `app/product/page.tsx` was an `async` component that awaited `getInventory()` (which calls `connection()`, forcing dynamic rendering) before rendering anything. This blocked the entire page — including the static `

Premium Widget

` title — until the inventory data resolved. The fix: I split the dynamic inventory into its own async `` component wrapped in a `` boundary. Now the page itself is no longer async, so the static title and shell stream immediately on navigation, while the inventory data loads in the background and streams in when ready.
